elements.element: Transition assistance obligation triggered on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Array shall (A) ... provide reasonable transition assistance to Ono"

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months"

elements.element: Transition assistance provided at then-current rates
elements.evidence: No rate mechanic; only "including continuing to supply Materials on the terms of Article IX" — no "then-current rates" language anywhere in the insertion

elements.element: Return of Customer Data (our Data/Confidential Information)
elements.evidence: "return to Ono ... all Data and other Confidential Information of Ono in Array's possession or control"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
Return within 30 days of expiry or termination (not conditioned on a later request)
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after Ono's written request" — the 30-day clock runs from a request, not from expiry or termination
"thereafter delete or destroy all remaining copies ... and certify such deletion or destruction to Ono in writing"

elements.element: At least 90 days of transition assistance
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months" exceeds 90 days
"within thirty (30) days after Ono's written request, return to Ono, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all Data"

offending_extra_words: including continuing to supply Materials on the terms of Article IX for so long as Ono is required to distribute the Product under Section 14.2(a)(ii)
subject to Array's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes
reasons: Locked target was preferred, but the insertion omits the "then-current rates" element of the transition obligation entirely, so the preferred bargain is incomplete.

The 30-day data-return clock runs "after Ono's written request" rather than from expiry or termination; a request condition should not gate/postpone the mandatory return deadline under the preferred position.
The clause does land squarely on the fallback (six months of assistance exceeds 90 days; 30-day machine-readable export), so it is acceptable at the fallback level.

Minimality fails: the insertion bolts on an unrequested continued-supply obligation tied to Article IX and Section 14.2(a)(ii), and adds an archival-copy carve-out that dilutes the deletion/certification protection the rule requires.

Intent is preserved: the new sub-paragraph (x) is appended after 14.2(a)(ix) without altering existing sentences, and it uses defined terms (Data, Confidential Information, Product, Wind-down/Article IX cross-references) already in the agreement.
